title: Jude and the Will
premise: Retired detective Xanthe Ravensworth has built a quiet life around a failing bookshop in the coastal town of Marrow Bay, until a confession letter arrives for 'Jude'—a name no one alive should know—postmarked the day after wealthy matriarch Edith Vane's funeral. The letter claims Edith's death was murder and points to three 'accidents' from thirty years ago that Xanthe once quietly proved were killings. As Xanthe peels back alibis woven across decades, they discover the letter-writer is Edith herself, mailed before her death to force one last reckoning—and that the killer, now a beloved town pillar, knows exactly who Jude is. In the end, Xanthe must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the found family of misfits who have become their only home; they choose truth, but on their own terms, letting the town believe what it needs while ensuring the killer can never hide again.
about_author: Xanthe Dunmore spent fifteen years as a court stenographer in northern England before turning to crime fiction, a career that taught her how people lie when their lives depend on it. She lives above a secondhand bookshop with two ill-tempered cats and writes her novels longhand.

chapters.title: The Postmark Problem
chapters.summary: Xanthe Ravensworth's POV. Days after Edith Vane's grand funeral, a letter arrives addressed to 'Jude'—Xanthe's buried birth name—confessing to murder and postmarked after death. Xanthe burns dinner, forgets to open the shop, and feels thirty years of careful invisibility crack. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in the eerie intimacy of being known by a dead woman.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, One Detective
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV, with flashbacks. We learn how Xanthe, as a young constable, quietly proved three deaths—a fall, a drowning, a fire—were murders, then was forced into silence by powerful families. All three victims were connected to the Vane estate. Emotional beat: old shame resurfacing; the cost of staying invisible.

chapters.title: The Reading Circle
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Priya, Xanthe's teenage shop assistant, who notices Xanthe unraveling and starts her own amateur investigation through the shop's gossip network. She maps who attended Edith's funeral against who benefited from the old will. Emotional beat: fierce loyalty; found family forming around a closed-off mentor.

chapters.title: Alibis Woven Thirty Years Ago
chapters.summary: Xanthe interviews the funeral's mourners: Edith's nephew Charles, now a judge; family lawyer Margaret Hale; gardener Tom Okafor. Each alibi is airtight—too airtight, rehearsed across decades. A torn photograph in Edith's effects shows four young people at the estate, one face scratched out. Emotional beat: mounting paranoia; everyone lies beautifully.

chapters.title: What the Will Says
chapters.summary: Margaret Hale's POV. The lawyer reads a sealed addendum to Edith's will: a trust contingent on 'Jude Ravensworth coming forward within ninety days.' Margaret realizes Edith orchestrated everything from beyond the grave. She says nothing—but someone saw her read it. Emotional beat: complicity; power corrupting even the dutiful.

chapters.title: The Scratched-Out Face
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Using photo restoration software, Priya recovers the scratched face: a fifth companion no record acknowledges—Edith's ward, declared dead in 1994. Meanwhile Xanthe's bookshop is ransacked, the letter stolen. Emotional beat: protective rage; the stakes turn personal and physical.

chapters.title: Ninety Days
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The clock ticks: whoever holds the letter also holds proof of Xanthe's identity. Xanthe traces the ward's fate to a boathouse fire—the fourth 'accident'—and realizes Edith witnessed it, carried the guilt for thirty years, and wrote the confession as a trap she knew would outlive her. Emotional beat: grim clarity; grief braided with resolve.

chapters.title: The Judge's Chamber
chapters.summary: Charles Vane's POV. Cornered by Xanthe's quiet questions, Charles reveals his version: the ward was blackmailing the family, and someone acted to protect them all. He believes Margaret did it; Margaret believes he did. His composure fractures, showing how thirty years of respectability curdled into rot. Emotional beat: the banality of corrupted power.

chapters.title: Marrow Bay Burns Twice
chapters.summary: Climax. Xanthe's POV. Lured to the restored boathouse by a forged note, Xanthe confronts the true killer—Tom Okafor, the gentle gardener, who killed to protect Edith's secret and now must erase Jude again. Priya arrives; the fire starts; Xanthe chooses saving Priya over the evidence, and Tom confesses in the smoke, believing them both doomed. Emotional beat: terror, sacrifice, and the confession finally spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Jude
chapters.summary: Resolution. Xanthe's POV. Tom survives, arrested; the police credit luck, not Xanthe, who lets the town keep its comfortable story. Xanthe formally claims the name Jude—not erasing the past but integrating it—and reopens the bookshop with Priya as partner. The last page: a new letter arrives, unsigned, reading only 'Thank you.' Emotional beat: quiet rebirth; identity chosen, family kept, justice imperfect but real.
